dividers.title: HOW IT WORKS
dividers.caption: ONE LOST CHECK IS NOT RED.

panels.title: ABOUT
panels.text: **synthwerk-pulse** is the platform's view of itself. It checks every service and infra part from `targets.yaml` and streams a stable status per target over Server-Sent Events.

items.label: LIMIT TO SHOW A STOPPED PART

items.title: CHECK
items.text: Kind http sends GET to a URL. Kind tcp connects to host:port. One target per box.

items.title: HOLD
items.text: A status changes only after a run of equal results. One lost check stays green.

items.title: STREAM
items.text: Server-Sent Events: a snapshot first, then one event per change. A ping every 15 s.
Pulse reads `SYNTHWERK_PULSE_TARGETS_FILE` at start. No API adds a target. Max 64 targets.
A `/readyz` body from `openapi/_shared/health.yaml` gives status and checks. Other 2xx or 3xx is ok.
A 4xx, a 5xx, a timeout or a refused connection is down. Pulse follows no redirect.
Opens a TCP connection to `host:port`. For parts without a health endpoint, such as Postgres.
The last status per target sits in `pulse_target_status`. The event goes to the outbox in the same transaction.
Compose infra targets poll every 5 s. A stopped part shows as down in about 10 to 15 s.

panels.title: QUICK START
lines: # stop a container: a status event says down

rows.text: Status, check, target, stream and monitor tests in `tests/unit`. No Docker.
Store, outbox and live status against real Postgres and NATS. Needs Docker.
Build the container image as CI builds it.
gofmt, golangci-lint, actionlint and zizmor.

items.text: Go 1.27. Docker for `just test-int` and `just image`. `just` runs the same commands as CI.
Start from `targets.example.yaml`. Set the targets file, database URL and NATS URL.

panels.title: ONE CHECK, LEFT TO RIGHT
panels.caption: A change goes to the open streams at once, also when Postgres is down.

items.text: After 2 down results in a row, from any status.
From down to ok or degraded after 3 results in a row that are not down.
From ok to degraded at once. Back to ok after 2 ok results in a row.
From unknown to ok or degraded after 1 result that is not down.
No event again: pulse writes an event only when the stored status differs.

rows.text: Liveness of the process.
Readiness. `postgres` and `nats` are critical.
The snapshot as one JSON document.
SSE: `snapshot` first, then `status` per change, `: ping` every 15 s. Max 50 streams, then 503. 1 h lifetime.
`http://127.0.0.1:8080/pulse/v1/health/stream`

items.text: `dev.synthwerk.pulse.target.status_changed.v1`, one per stored change.
Transactional outbox to NATS JetStream stream `EVT_PULSE`, with the Go kit from synthwerk-contracts `go/v0.1.0`.

rows.text: Postgres URL. Required. A secret: never in the repo.
NATS JetStream URL.
The targets file. Read at start.
Listen address. Default `:8080`.
Check interval. Default `15s`. 1 s to 5 min.
Check timeout. Default `3s`. Max the interval and 10 s.
Max open streams. Default `50`.
Environment name, such as `local`.
Log level.
Log format.
OTLP endpoint for traces, gRPC.

items.text: The local edge binds to `127.0.0.1`. The operator role check comes with identity.
No leader lock and no fan-out over `sys.health.>` yet.
Pulse uses `pulse_` tables in the shared database. Its own database comes with the infra module.
No incidents, metrics, alerts, KPIs or audit consumer.

rows.text: status, check, target, stream, monitor.
testcontainers Postgres + NATS: outbox events checked against the contract schemas, live down and up over SSE.
Blueprint go-ci: gofmt, golangci-lint, `go test -race`, build.
Build, SBOM, Trivy. On main and tags: push to `ghcr.io/velimirmueller/synthwerk-pulse`, sign with cosign.
One required check over all jobs.

code:
# in synthwerk-infra
scripts/init-env.sh && docker compose up --wait
curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8080/pulse/v1/health/stream

# in synthwerk-pulse
just test-unit    # unit tests, no Docker
just test-int     # Postgres + NATS, needs Docker
just image        # container image as CI builds it

just lint         # gofmt, golangci-lint, actionlint, zizmor
just test-unit    # go test -race ./tests/unit/...
just test-int     # go test -tags integration -race ./tests/integration/...
